LHCb Upgrade II · PicoCal Optical Readout Uniformity & Inverse Problem Study

Reconstructing Micron-Scale Light-Guide Surface Imperfections from 2D Laser Scans

Author: Hengne Li (李衡讷) | Hengne.Li@cern.ch | Hengne.Li@m.scnu.edu.cn · SCNU / CERN LHCb

To explain and quantitatively reproduce the non-uniform 2D light-yield ripples observed across a 4-cell conical light guide (Ø17.5 mm entrance → Ø8.0 mm exit, 100 mm length), we formulated a 576-DOF periodic bicubic B-spline freeform surface model coupled with native Apple Metal GPU ray tracing and zero-free-parameter Geant4 11.1.3 optical validation (97.6%–98.0% absolute scale agreement), recovering -268 μm to +272 μm machining/film bulges with pixel-level fidelity.

SECTION 01

Physical Diagnosis: Why Micron-Scale Wall Bulges Create Strong 2D Scan Ripples

Quantitative diagnosis combining STEP CAD geometry and 10,000-point diffuse laser scan measurements

1. Experimental Geometry & Sub-Pixel Calibration

Parsing 4cells_17.5mm_8mm_circle_to_circle_100mm-Cut.step and fitting an error-function edge model to scan_summary.csv (100 × 100 grid, 0.2 mm pitch) establishes:

  • Nominal Tapered Cone: Length L = 100.0 mm, entrance R_in = 8.75 mm, exit R_out = 4.00 mm, half-angle α = 2.72°, coupled to an 8.18 mm PMT bore.
  • Reflective Film Thickness: Calibrated optical aperture R_eff = 8.438 mm (~311 μm inward offset matching reflective foil thickness); laser spot σ_beam = 0.219 mm.
  • Non-Axisymmetric Ripples: Around the 25.4 mV plateau, a -5.5% dark pit appears at (X' ≈ -0.8, Y' ≈ +1.8) mm alongside a +3.5% to +5.0% right crescent.

2. Critical-Angle Lever Effect in Conical Concentrators

Phase-space etendue conservation restricts maximum diffuse collection to the area ratio (4.00 / 8.75)² ≈ 20.9%:

Polar angle increment per wall bounce: θ_(k+1) ≈ θ_k + 2·(α + Δα_local)
  • >99% Multi-Bounce Transport: Fewer than 1% of photons reach the exit directly; guided photons undergo 1–14 specular bounces while ~78% turn around (dz < 0) and escape.
  • Slope-Induced Escape & Refocusing: A 150–200 μm inward bulge steepens the upstream slope (+Δα), forcing near-critical rays into early turnaround escape (dark pit), while gentler downstream slopes rescue rays (bright band).
SECTION 02

Methodology: Freeform Surface Parameterization & Fast Inverse Solver

Combining C² analytic surface normals, 300M rays/s Metal GPU throughput, Geant4 validation, and strict memory safety

01

Periodic Bicubic B-Spline

Eliminates facet-crease artifacts via smooth cylindrical B-splines:

R(θ, z) = R_CAD(z) + ΔR_axi(z) + ΔR(θ, z)
  • 36 azimuthal × 16 axial = 576 C²-continuous control DOFs;
  • Exact analytic partial derivatives yield true 3D inward normal n(θ, z);
  • Concentric reference cone per bounce forces quadratic C ≡ 0, preventing self-hit.
02

Native Apple Metal GPU

Compiled Objective-C++ & Metal Compute Shader (libmetal_raytracer.dylib):

  • Scrambled 2D Sobol QMC hemispherical diffuse emission at each (X, Y) scan point;
  • Inline bicubic evaluation + 4-step Newton root refinement + up to 20 specular bounces;
  • Sustains ~300M multi-bounce rays/s on Apple M3 Max.
03

SO(2) Equivariant Inversion

Three-stage lightweight solver avoiding multi-GB autodiff graph unrolling:

  • Stage 1: Fit radial profile to lock axisymmetric reflective film offset;
  • Stage 2: Exploit rotational symmetry—perturb only 16 axial basis modes to assemble the full 576-DOF Jacobian in ~3 s;
  • Stage 3: Laplacian curvature regularization + exact GPU backtracking line search.
04

Geant4 11.1.3 Cross-Check

Independent optical Monte Carlo verification via local envs/g4:

  • Export watertight G4TessellatedSolid (56,576 facets) with polished dielectric_metal mirror;
  • 5 parallel workers shooting 120,000 G4OpticalPhoton tracks (~11 s runtime, 97.6%–98.0% match);
  • MemoryGuard enforces hard RSS ceiling (peak only 334.9 MB).
INDEPENDENT PARTICLE-PHYSICS CROSS-VALIDATION · ZERO RE-TUNED PARAMETERS

✅ Geant4 11.1.3 Independent Cross-Validation Conclusion: 97.6%–98.0% Absolute Agreement

Passing the reconstructed B-spline surface mesh, mirror reflectivity, cosine angular exponent, and PMT voltage gain directly into Geant4 11.1.3 (G4OpticalPhysics + G4TessellatedSolid) with zero parameter re-tuning confirms both the absolute light-collection scale and the transverse 'double-peak flanking a central-left dip' spatial waveform along Y' = +1.60 mm (15 points × 8,000 photons = 120,000 optical photons).

Physical Origin of the ~2.4% (-0.63 mV) Offset:

  • 50 μm PMT Overlap-Safety Air Gap (~-1.5% to -2.0%): ray-tracer.py scores photons directly at z = 100.00 mm, whereas geant4-light-guide.cc places PmtWindowPV front face at z = 100.05 mm to prevent volume-overlap warnings, letting grazing high-angle exit rays slip outside R = 8.18 mm.
  • Planar Facets vs. Smooth C² Spline (~±1% jitter): The fast 11 s Geant4 check uses a 60(θ) × 61(z) planar facet mesh (6° steps); over 4–8 bounces, facet-normal jumps add ~0.3–0.5 mV caustic jitter, nudging pure-stat χ²/ndf from 1.0 to 1.89.
  • Point Source vs. Finite Laser Spot: Geant4 shoots an ideal point source while experiment & primary simulation convolve the σ_beam = 0.219 mm spot. (Green Geant4 points are live-overlaid in Section 03 below!)
